about.title: Smouldering peat, detected before the flames show
about.tagline: In Indonesian, asap means smoke. We make sure responders hear about it ASAP, and know it's real.
about.lede: ASAPify detects smouldering — fire below the peat surface that has not yet burned vegetation — across all of Kalimantan's peatland. It is early detection of combustion, not risk prediction.
about.step1_d: Himawari-9 and GK2A observe the same peat pixels independently, at night only (20:00–04:00 WIB).
about.step2_d: Multi-Attribute Utility Theory (MAUT) combines both satellites' thermal anomalies, skin and air temperature, and 3-night consistency.
about.step3_d: AWAS needs support from ≥ 2 of 8 neighbours and agreement from both satellites. An isolated anomaly is at most Watch.
about.step4_d: An ADK + Gemini agent checks VIIRS detections and VIIRS/Himawari imagery for each AWAS cluster. The result is strong evidence or inconclusive.
about.step5_d: An operator publishes or rejects. Only published alerts are sent by the bot to the provincial Telegram group, one way.
about.ai_body: Satellites and transparent rules detect; neighbours validate; AI only verifies AWAS candidates; humans make the call. AI never changes a status.
about.maut_body: U = Σ wᵢuᵢ / Σ wᵢ over the available attributes. Attributes from a cloudy satellite are dropped. Initial values, calibrated on the 2023 backtest.
about.st_awas: U ≥ 0.65, ≥ 2 of 8 neighbours support, and Himawari + GK2A agree
about.st_watch: U ≥ 0.30 but not AWAS (includes isolated or single-satellite anomalies)
about.st_noobs: Both satellites cloudy or no data. Cloud = missing data, not safe
about.sat_h: Himawari-9 AHI (JMA, Japan) · 140.7° E · B07 3.9 µm + B14 11.2 µm
about.sat_g: GEO-KOMPSAT-2A AMI (KMA, Korea) · 128.2° E · SW038 3.8 µm + IR105 10.5 µm
about.sat_note: The 3.8–3.9 µm channel is about 25× more sensitive to embers than the 11 µm channel, and nights are free of solar reflection.
about.limit1: Only smouldering large enough for a ~2 km pixel is detected.
about.limit2: Cloud = no data. Safe status cannot be confirmed under cloud.
about.limit3: VIIRS true-colour imagery exists only in daytime; night smoke is not visible.
about.limit4: NASA POWER is coarse (0.5°) and ~1.5 days late, so it is used only as a baseline.
about.data_note: Himawari-9 and GK2A from NOAA open data. All processing runs on Google Cloud (Cloud Run, Vertex AI Gemini, ADK, Firestore, Cloud Storage).
